properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean foundation composed of Lower Carboniferous sedimentary bedrock belonging to the Strathclyde Group, comprising interbedded blonde sandstones, carbonaceous siltstones, and mudstones overlain by dense glacial till. Primary architectural masonry sourced from local Craigleith and Hailes quarries: fine-to-medium-grained quartz-arenite sandstone with high silica content and carbonaceous laminations. Pedestal foundation blocks utilize polished Peterhead pink granite atop dressed Craigleith bedrock pads. Mortar matrices consist of traditional non-hydraulic lime binders blended with sharp, coarse quartz sands, showing localized modern repointing with natural hydraulic lime (NHL 2.0). Groundwater dynamics governed by shallow seasonal perched water tables beneath parkland topsoil.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Enclosed urban park lawn (*Lolium perenne*, *Festuca rubra*) showing winter dormancy. Deciduous canopy consisting of mature *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime), *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore), and *Platanus × acerifolia* (London Plane). Phenology precisely aligned with late December (2026-12-22): 100% defoliation; bare, highly articulated branch architecture; dormant winter buds; dark, wet-barked trunks with localized epiphytic crustose lichens (*Lecanora*) and moss cushions (*Hypnum cupressiforme*) on prevailing weather flanks.

properties.architectural_summary: Neoclassical urban ensemble comprising Robert Adam's uniform residential palace-front terraces (1791–1820) and Robert Reid’s central West Register House (formerly St George's Church, 1811–1814). West Register House features a monumental centralized copper-clad dome on an arcaded drum with Corinthian pilasters, surmounting a rusticated ashlar base with an advanced tetrastyle Ionic portico and flanking pavilion wings. Flanking terraced townhouses adhere to strict symmetrical Georgian orders: rusticated ground-floor ashlar over sunken basements, smooth-dressed piano nobile with pedimented and molded architraves, second-storey square windows, and continuous balustraded parapets. Roofscapes feature pitched slate-clad timber rafters with lead-dressed dormers, chimney stacks with ceramic pots, and ashlar skew copings. Central park features the Prince Albert Memorial (1876, Sir John Steell): bronze equestrian monument atop an ornate stepped granite pedestal with secondary bronze allegorical relief groups at the corners.
